chunks: O you who believe, do not be like those who maligned Moses, whilst God cleared him of what they alleged; and he was held in high esteem with God.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of God clearing Moses from the slander of his people in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as a direct parallel to the slander against Aisha bint Abi Bakr, emphasizing that just as God purified Moses (AS) from the accusations of the Israelites, He protected the Prophet’s household from false narratives. The term 'wajihan' (elevated status) underscores the spiritual purity and high rank of the Prophet and his family, reinforcing the concept of Ismah (infallibility) in key figures. This serves as a foundational argument for the divine protection of the Ahl al-Bayt from major sins and errors in judgment.
